text: Amenorrhea: Amenorrhea or amenorrhoea is the absence of a menstrual period in a female organism which has reached reproductive age. Physiological states of amenorrhea are most commonly seen during pregnancy and lactation (breastfeeding).

Delayed puberty: Delayed puberty is when a person lacks or has incomplete development of specific sexual characteristics past the usual age of onset of puberty. The person may have no physical or hormonal signs that puberty has begun.
Dysmenorrhea: Dysmenorrhea, also known as period pain, painful periods or menstrual cramps, is pain during menstruation. Its usual onset occurs around the time that menstruation begins.
Dyspareunia: Dyspareunia is painful sexual intercourse. Although dyspareunia can occur in all human bodies, it is most commonly observed in people with vulvas.
Galactorrhea: Galactorrhea or lactorrhea is the spontaneous flow of milk from the breast, unassociated with childbirth or nursing.

Heavy menstrual bleeding: Heavy menstrual bleeding (HMB), previously known as menorrhagia or hematomunia, is a menstrual period with excessively heavy flow. It is a type of abnormal uterine bleeding (AUB).
Hirsutism: Hirsutism is excessive body hair on parts of the body where hair is normally absent or minimal. The word is from the early 17th century: from Latin hirsutus meaning "hairy".
Infertility: In biology, infertility is the inability of a male and female organism to reproduce. It is usually not the natural state of a healthy organism that has reached sexual maturity.

Intermenstrual bleeding: Intermenstrual bleeding (IMB), or metrorrhagia, is abnormal vaginal bleeding at irregular intervals between expected menstrual periods. It may be associated with bleeding with sexual intercourse.

Irregular vaginal bleeding: Intermenstrual bleeding (IMB), or metrorrhagia, is abnormal vaginal bleeding at irregular intervals between expected menstrual periods. It may be associated with bleeding with sexual intercourse.

Oligomenorrhea: Oligomenorrhea is an abnormal bleeding pattern where menstrual bleeding occurs at intervals of greater than 35 days, with fewer than 9 periods in a year. The period may be light in flow, short in duration or occur at irregular intervals.

Polymenorrhea: Polymenorrhea, also known as frequent periods, frequent menstruation, or frequent menstrual bleeding, is a menstrual disorder in which menstrual cycles are shorter than 21 days in length and hence where menstruation occurs more frequently than usual. Cycles are regular and menstrual flow is normal in the condition.
Post menopausal bleeding: A presenting complaint characterised by post menopausal bleeding.

Precocious puberty: In medicine, precocious puberty is puberty occurring at an unusually early age. In most cases, the process is normal in every aspect except the unusually early age and simply represents a variation of normal development.

Vaginal discharge: Vaginal discharge is a mixture of liquid, cells, and bacteria that lubricate and protect the vagina. This mixture is constantly produced by the cells of the vagina and cervix, and it exits the body through the vaginal opening.
Vulval soreness: A presenting complaint characterised by vulval soreness.

Common presenting complaints: Irregular Vaginal Bleeding. Associated symptoms: Irregular, Abnormally Frequent, Prolonged, Or Excessive Amounts Of Uterine Bleeding. Risk factors: Ovulation Problems, Fibroids, Lining Of The Uterus Growing Into The Uterine Wall, Uterine Polyps, Underlying Bleeding Problems, Side Effects From Birth Control, Cancer. Age relevance: . Sex relevance: . Acute or chronic: .

Abnormal uterine and vaginal bleeding, unspecified red flags. Red flag (RF_HEMODYNAMIC_INSTABILITY) triggered by symptom 'PROLONGED': Prolonged or heavy bleeding with symptoms of hemodynamic compromise.

Abnormal uterine and vaginal bleeding, unspecified differential diagnosis notes. Compared to Irregular Menstruation Unspecified: Abnormal uterine/vaginal bleeding is the broader bleeding-pattern code; irregular menstruation unspecified emphasizes cycle-timing irregularity specifically

Acute vaginitis: A female-genital-reproductive condition known as Acute vaginitis. Common presenting complaints: Vaginal Discharge. Associated symptoms: Itching, Burning, Pain, Discharge, Bad Smell. Acute vaginitis differential diagnosis notes. Compared to Subacute And Chronic Vaginitis: Acute vaginitis has sudden onset over days; chronic vaginitis has symptoms persisting beyond ~4 weeks or recurring Compared to Postmenopausal Atrophic Vaginitis: Atrophic vaginitis occurs in postmenopausal women with low estrogen, typically dryness rather than infective discharge Compared to Vaginitis Following Delivery: Postpartum timing (within 6 weeks of delivery) distinguishes vaginitis following delivery

Congenital adrenal hyperplasia: Congenital adrenal hyperplasia (CAH) is a group of autosomal recessive disorders characterized by impaired cortisol synthesis. It results from the deficiency of one of the five enzymes required for the synthesis of cortisol in the adrenal cortex. Common presenting complaints: Precocious Puberty. Associated symptoms: none listed. Risk factors: none listed. Age relevance: . Sex relevance: . Acute or chronic: .

Cushing syndrome, unspecified: Cushing's syndrome is a collection of signs and symptoms due to prolonged exposure to glucocorticoids such as cortisol. Signs and symptoms may include high blood pressure, abdominal obesity but with thin arms and legs, reddish stretch marks, a round red face due to facial plethora, a fat lump between the shoulders, weak muscles, weak bones, acne, and fragile skin that heals poorly. Common presenting complaints: Hirsutism. Associated symptoms: none listed. Risk factors: none listed. Age relevance: . Sex relevance: . Acute or chronic: .
Cushing syndrome, unspecified red flags. Red flag (RF_CUSHINGOID_RAPID_ONSET) triggered by disease 'CUSHING_SYNDROME_UNSPECIFIED': Rapidly progressive Cushingoid features with new-onset hypertension.

Hypogonadotropic hypogonadism: Hypogonadotropic hypogonadism (HH), is a disorder where the pituitary gland fails to produce the required levels of the hormones which are needed to stimulate the gonads to function normally. This usually means that the gonads produce unusually low levels of sex hormones, but it can also lead to other functional problems such as insufficient sperm in male HH. Common presenting complaints: Delayed Puberty. Associated symptoms: none listed. Risk factors: none listed. Age relevance: . Sex relevance: . Acute or chronic: .
Hypogonadotropic hypogonadism red flags. Red flag (RF_NO_PUBERTY_BY_13_15) triggered by disease 'HYPOGONADOTROPIC_HYPOGONADISM': No breast development by 13 or no menarche by 15.

Hypogonadotropic hypogonadism differential diagnosis notes. Compared to Turner Syndrome: Hypogonadotropic hypogonadism shows low FSH/LH; Turner syndrome typically shows elevated FSH/LH (hypergonadotropic) with confirmed karyotype abnormality

Idiopathic hirsutism differential diagnosis notes. Compared to Cushing Syndrome Unspecified: Idiopathic hirsutism has normal cortisol/androgen work-up; Cushing's syndrome shows biochemical cortisol excess plus systemic features

Other vulvodynia: Vulvodynia is a chronic pain condition that affects the vulvar area and occurs without an identifiable cause. Symptoms typically include a feeling of burning or irritation. Polycystic ovarian syndrome: Polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS), previously called polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), is the most common hormonal disorder in women of reproductive age. Common presenting complaints: Hirsutism. Associated symptoms: none listed. Risk factors: none listed. Age relevance: . Sex relevance: . Acute or chronic: .

Polycystic ovarian syndrome red flags. Red flag (RF_RAPID_VIRILIZATION) triggered by complaint 'HIRSUTISM': Rapid-onset virilization atypical for PCOS, raising suspicion of an androgen-secreting tumor.

Polycystic ovarian syndrome differential diagnosis notes. Compared to Idiopathic Hirsutism: PCOS shows irregular cycles/ovulatory dysfunction and characteristic ultrasound/biochemical findings; idiopathic hirsutism has regular ovulatory cycles and normal androgen levels Compared to Cushing Syndrome Unspecified: Cushing's syndrome shows additional features (central obesity, striae, proximal weakness) and abnormal cortisol testing, distinguishing it from PCOS-related hirsutism

Precocious puberty, central differential diagnosis notes. Heavy bleeding with hemodynamic instability - action: Emergency referral / call ambulance.
Suspected ectopic pregnancy (positive pregnancy test with pelvic pain/bleeding) - action: Emergency referral for urgent beta-hCG and pelvic ultrasound.
Any bleeding occurring after confirmed menopause - action: Urgent 2-week-wait gynecology referral to rule out endometrial malignancy.
Persistent bleeding, unexplained weight loss, or palpable pelvic mass - action: Urgent 2-week-wait gynecology-oncology referral.
Fever, severe pelvic pain, and tachycardia suggestive of PID with sepsis - action: Same-day urgent assessment; consider IV antibiotics and admission.
Sudden severe unilateral pelvic pain with nausea/vomiting - action: Emergency surgical referral.
Rapid-onset virilization (voice deepening, clitoromegaly, rapid hair growth progression) - action: Urgent endocrinology referral to rule out androgen-secreting tumor.
Precocious puberty with headache, visual disturbance, or rapid tempo - action: Urgent pediatric endocrinology referral; consider MRI brain.
Heavy bleeding with dizziness, pallor, breathlessness, or tachycardia - action: Urgent referral for hemoglobin check and possible transfusion.
Galactorrhea with visual field defect or persistent severe headache - action: Urgent MRI pituitary and endocrinology referral.
Rapidly progressive Cushingoid features with new hypertension - action: Urgent endocrinology referral.
Genital symptoms in a child/adolescent raising safeguarding concern - action: Safeguarding referral per local child-protection protocol.
No breast development by age 13, or no menarche by age 15 - action: Referral to pediatric endocrinology.
Known/suspected Turner syndrome with cardiac symptoms or murmur - action: Cardiology referral for echocardiogram (coarctation/aortic root risk).
Infertility work-up patient presenting with acute pelvic pain - action: Urgent gynecology assessment to exclude ectopic pregnancy or torsion.
